short: Its defeat saved England from invasion and marked a shift in European naval warfare.
full:
In July 1588, a fleet of 130 ships dispatched by Philip II of Spain arrived in the English Channel. The Armada's objective was to escort an invasion force from Flanders to overthrow Queen Elizabeth I and restore Catholicism in England. Under the command of the Duke of Medina Sidonia, the fleet maintained a tight crescent formation that English galleons initially struggled to penetrate, despite their superior maneuverability and long-range artillery.

The campaign culminated at the Battle of Gravelines on 8 August. English fireships broke the Spanish formation, forcing individual vessels into chaotic engagements. Prevented from joining the invasion army, the Armada was driven into the North Sea and forced to return to Spain by sailing around Scotland and Ireland. Severe storms wrecked dozens of ships on the treacherous coasts, costing Spain over sixty vessels and thousands of men. The survival of Protestant England dealt a severe blow to Spanish prestige, though the broader war continued for another sixteen years.
